item.title: Inside Tech Week 2026: Partnering Early With the Companies Building What's Next
item.description: At Tech Week, Morgan Stanley's senior leaders meet directly with founders, investors and technology partners to engage early with the shifts reshaping financial services and to begin relationships that grow across the integrated firm.

item.title: The Next Stage of the Market Correction
item.description: Is the end of the correction in sight? Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist looks at what could bring this pullback to an end.

item.title: The Undervalued Companies Benefiting from AI
item.description: Morgan Stanley Research mapped its global coverage of about 3,600 stocks to identify how the next phase of AI investing could broaden beyond technology enablers.

item.title: Dan Ivascyn: Conviction Needs Capital
item.description: Dan Ivascyn, Group Chief Investment Officer at PIMCO, joined Morgan Stanley’s Co-President Dan Simkowitz for a deep dive on his experiences during the global financial crisis. He shared how an early underweight on mortgage-backed securities was the right call at the wrong time, and how he ultimately benefited from taking on risk as markets recovered.

item.title: A Narrower Path for Growth and Stability
item.description: Higher rates can take time to filter through the economy, making their full impact difficult to judge. Arunima Sinha from our U.S. and Global Economics team considers where the pressure may emerge next and how policymakers could navigate the competing risks.

item.title: Squawk on the Street: Ted Pick on AI, Geopolitics and the Firm’s Strong Performance in the Third Quarter
item.description: In a full video interview with CNBC’s Leslie Picker on “Squawk on the Street,” Morgan Stanley Chairman and CEO Ted Pick shares his view of current market backdrop—including how advances in artificial intelligence, shifting geopolitical dynamics and changing expectations for inflation and interest rates could influence markets heading into the fourth quarter.

item.title: AI Boom Faces a Higher-Yield Roadblock
item.description: Our ABS Strategist Carolyn Campbell explains how rising borrowing costs are slowing the AI data center boom and what could drive a rebound in financing.

item.title: Healthcare's Next Growth Drivers: M&A, Innovation and AI
item.description: How healthcare leaders are navigating patent expirations, healthcare M&A and AI adoption to shape the future of the industry.

item.title: How AI and Tokenization Could Reshape Wealth Management
item.description: Betsy Graseck and Michael Cyprys explore how AI could expand advisor capacity and tokenized assets could grow into a $2.3 trillion market by 2030.

item.title: 4 Market Signals Ahead of the Midterms
item.description: As investors look toward the U.S. midterm elections, the biggest question is what could change. Our Head of U.S. Public Policy Research Ariana Salvatore outlines the signals worth watching.

item.title: China’s $12 Trillion Manufacturing Upgrade
item.description: Our China Industrials Analyst Sheng Zhong explains how AI, robotics and a major investment cycle could transform China’s manufacturing base and its role in global supply chains.

item.title: The Stock Market’s Bad Breadth
item.description: Fewer companies have been driving equity market gains in 2026. Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson looks at what investors should make of the narrowing rally as the year enters its final stretch.

item.title: Why the Biggest AI Opportunity Is Still Ahead
item.description: AI’s next wave may reward companies using the technology most effectively—not just those building it. Here’s what investors can watch as AI moves toward profits.

item.title: The Midterm Election Signals Investors Should Watch
item.description: Affordability concerns are shaping the election backdrop, with implications for policy expectations and sectors such as technology and energy.

item.title: Market Resilience Isn’t Complacency
item.description: Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson discusses why quality stocks, strong earnings and price momentum support his view that the bull market remains intact.

item.title: Can Stocks Keep Defying Higher Rates?
item.description: Stocks are climbing on strong earnings and artificial intelligence investment, but rising rates and consumer stress could test the rally.

item.title: The Robot Almanac: Introduction to Physical AI
item.description: See what happens as AI evolves beyond software to move, build, drive and fly. Machines can now sense and interact with the world around them. Morgan Stanley Research explains why robotics could become one of the most important technology and investment themes of the coming decades—and where adoption may accelerate first.

item.title: Why the Middle-Class Squeeze Is Getting Worse
item.description:
Heather Berger of the U.S. Economics Team hosts Wealth Management Senior Economist and Strategist Sarah Wolfe to discuss what it takes to define the middle class in America today. They break down how factors like rising essential costs and the development of AI are reshaping consumer balance sheets and financial security.

Sarah Wolfe is a member of Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management Division and is not a member of Morgan Stanley’s Research Department. Unless otherwise indicated, her views are her own and may differ from the views of the Morgan Stanley Research Department and from the views of others within Morgan Stanley.

item.title: The Fed, Football and the Price of Ambiguity
item.description: Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets discusses when markets may not adequately compensate investors for uncertainty around themes like Fed policy, AI financing and energy supply.

item.title: What Could Shake Up Markets in September?
item.description: Investors have plenty to digest this month, from economic data to central-bank decisions. Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets outlines what could drive the next bout of volatility.

item.title: Brad Jacobs: Question Deeply, Act Quickly
item.description: In this episode of Hard Lessons, the Chairman and CEO of QXO and founder of Jacobs Private Equity shares how he has achieved success in more than 500 mergers and acquisitions. Watch for his take on how 1+1 can equal 11, when to disrespect the org chart and when to stop selling and start doing.

item.title: Markets Shrug as U.S. Debt Hits $40 Trillion
item.description: As government debt levels continue to rise around the world, investors are asking whether higher borrowing will weigh on economic growth or simply change how capital is allocated across markets.

item.title: Why Selectivity Matters in Today’s Markets
item.description: Higher rates and sharper scrutiny of AI investments are raising the bar for companies and rewarding discerning investors.

item.title: Why the Yen’s Next Move Depends on the Fed
item.description: The Japanese yen is sitting near its weakest level in more than three decades – and with implications for U.S. Treasury yields, borrowing costs and global market volatility.

item.title: Korean Stocks: From Correction to a Healthy Recovery
item.description: After a historic rally and a sharp correction, South Korea’s equity market may be approaching a turning point. Our Chief Korea Equity Strategist Joon Seok explains that the next cycle will need stronger foundations and more sectors joining in.

item.title: Equity Outlook: A Constructive Case for Stocks
item.description: Rising earnings expectations support a constructive outlook for equities through the end of 2026, despite ongoing market risks.

item.title: When AI Takes Over Shopping Carts
item.description: Our analysts Andrew Ruben and Nathan Feather discuss how AI shopping agents could transform how consumers discover, compare and buy products and the implications for eCommerce.

item.title: The UK Has a Better Story to Tell
item.description: Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets examines why investors might be overlooking the stability and performance of UK assets, despite persistent negative sentiment.

item.title: ‘Show Me the Money,’ Market Tells Companies
item.description: Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson discusses a new market cycle, in which investors are demanding more than just growth from companies.

item.title: Market Signals: Rates, Earnings and Private Markets
item.description: Our market signals for stocks, bonds and alternatives in the second half of 2026 indicate growth, inflation and interest rates should settle at higher levels.

item.title: When a Data Center Comes to Town
item.description:
Head of U.S. Public Policy Strategy Ariana Salvatore and U.S. Thematic Strategist Michelle Weaver, alongside Senior Economist and Strategist in Morgan Stanley’s Private Wealth Management Sarah Wolfe, examine the economics of the AI data center boom, the pushback and the policy implications.

Sarah Wolfe is a member of Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management Division and is not a member of Morgan Stanley’s Research Department. Unless otherwise indicated, her views are her own and may differ from the views of the Morgan Stanley Research Department and from the views of others within Morgan Stanley.

item.title: Quality Matters Again
item.description: Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson explains why investors should favor quality as the market moves from early-cycle momentum to more disciplined, mid-cycle leadership.

item.title: The Structural Forces Moving Capital
item.description: Our Strategist Michelle Weaver talks to Michael Zezas and Jessica Alsford, Co-Directors of the Morgan Stanley Institute, about how AI, energy resilience and industrial policy are changing investment decisions.

item.title: Blind Spots in the AI Infrastructure Selloff
item.description: Our Global Head of Thematic and Sustainability Research Stephen Byrd explains why the recent AI infrastructure selloff may reflect technical pressures, not weakening fundamentals.

item.title: The Oil Market’s Billion-Barrel Problem
item.description: How much runway does the world’s energy market still have? Our Head of Commodity Research Martijn Rats joins our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets to explain what’s causing pressure beyond renewed tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Fed in July: A Weaker Case for Hiking
item.description: Our Global Head of Macro Strategy Matthew Hornbach and Chief U.S. Economist Michael Gapen unpack what is likely to influence this week’s interest rate decision by the Fed.

item.title: A More Selective Stock Market
item.description: Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson explains why he thinks the bull market has entered a new phase, with more focus on quality.

item.title: An Odyssey Through Market History
item.description: Looking at clues from the past, our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets examines how the recurring themes—from deregulation to volatility—are shaping markets and why every cycle still takes its own path.

item.title: Watch Out for a Fed Pause
item.description: Markets are pricing at least one 2026 rate hike, but Morgan Stanley Research expects the Fed to stay on hold as inflation moderates, supporting Treasuries and high-quality fixed income.

item.title: What This Choppy Market Is Telling Investors
item.description: After a sharp rebound, high earnings expectations and fast rotations in Big Tech are keeping the market churning sideways. How should you invest?

item.title: What’s Fueling Stocks After the AI Trade
item.description: Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Officer Mike Wilson discusses where investors may find opportunity beyond the AI sector and risks that could slow market gains.

item.title: Jean Eric Salata: Find the Comeback in the Setback
item.description: The EQT Group Chair joined Mo Assomull, Morgan Stanley Global Co-Head of Investment Banking, to discuss his journey from managing a small Asia fund to leading one of the world’s largest global private markets firms that today spans the U.S., Europe and Asia. He shared how seeing the world as an outsider gives him an advantage and the importance of finding the comeback after a setback.

item.title: Next Leg of the Bull Market?
item.description: A changing macro backdrop is creating new opportunities across the equity market. Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson looks at what's driving the shift and where it may lead next.

item.title: What to Watch Ahead of the Midterms
item.description: With voters focused on prices and the economy, our Head of Public Policy Research Ariana Salvatore and U.S. Thematic Strategist Michelle Weaver discuss the consumer trends that could matter most heading into November’s elections.

item.title: Where Macro Meets Micro: Investing Through Structural Change
item.description: Morgan Stanley’s Macro ↔ Micro Markets Forum examined how AI, geopolitics and shifting capital flows are creating new opportunities across markets and asset classes.

item.title: The Market Shift Investors May Be Missing
item.description: Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson explains that gains in the stock market are expanding to more sectors and why investors should position quickly.

item.title: Comeback for Europe’s Bull Market?
item.description: Europe's equity rally has surprised many investors. Our Europe Head of Research Product Paul Walsh and Chief European Equity Strategist Marina Zavolock discuss potential outcomes of the broadening market.

item.title: The Warsh Effect on Mortgages
item.description: Although markets may recalibrate to a different policy playbook under the new Fed chair Kevin Warsh, housing could remain in a holding pattern. Our co-heads of Securitized Products Research Jay Bacow and James Egan explain why.

item.title: How AI, Capital Deployment and Consumer Resilience Are Reshaping Finance
item.description: Steady consumer trends, large-scale AI investment and the evolving role of private credit are driving new opportunities—and new competition—across financial institutions.

item.title: Consumer Confidence and the U.S. Midterms
item.description: Our U.S. Public Policy Strategist Ariana Salvatore joins our Deputy Global Head of Research Michael Zezas to consider the consumer outlook and how it may impact the November midterm elections.

item.title: What a Quieter Fed Could Mean for Markets
item.description: In his first meeting as Fed Chair, Kevin Warsh signaled restraint in providing guidance. Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets looks at possible impacts of the new approach.

item.title: The Obstacles to Buying a First Home
item.description:
First-time homebuyers may get short windows of relief, but our co-head of Securitized Products Research James Egan and Senior Economist and Strategist in Morgan Stanley's Private Wealth Management Sarah Wolfe say the bigger story is a housing market resetting around a higher bar to entry.

Sarah Wolfe is a member of Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management Division and is not a member of Morgan Stanley’s Research Department. Unless otherwise indicated, her views are her own and may differ from the views of the Morgan Stanley Research Department and from the views of others within Morgan Stanley.

item.title: Why Warsh May Let Markets Tough It Out
item.description: Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson reacts to Kevin Warsh’s first Fed meeting, explaining why the new chair’s credibility may require letting markets experience some short-term pain.

item.title: Inside the AI Debt Surge
item.description: As AI investment keeps growing, our strategists Carolyn Campbell and Vishwas Patkar discuss the many ways tech infrastructure gets financed and the opportunities for investors.

item.title: Can Policy Solve AI’s Chipflation?
item.description: AI’s appetite for memory has turned chips into an inflationary factor. Our U.S. Public Policy Strategist Ariana Salvatore looks at what policymakers could do to reduce that pressure.

item.title: Pet Owners Tighten the Leash on Spending
item.description: After years of strong growth, rising costs are prompting more selective pet spending and slowing industry expansion.

item.title: Warsh’s Opening Act at the Fed
item.description: Our Global Head of Macro Strategy Matthew Hornbach and our Chief U.S. Economist Michael Gapen discuss the signals investors will be seeking from the new Fed Chair leading his first monetary policy meeting and possible implications for markets.

item.title: The Bull Case After the Pullback in Stocks
item.description: Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson explains why the recent equity correction may be more reset than reversal and where investors may find the next opportunities as leadership shifts.

item.title: India’s Next Market Phase
item.description: Chief Asia Economist Chetan Ahya joins Head of India Research and Chief India Equity Strategist Ridham Desai to break down India’s macro outlook, capital flows and sector opportunities.

item.title: Inflation Relief Ahead?
item.description: Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets explains our differentiated view of a potential benign outlook for inflation, despite the recent acceleration.

item.title: Who Owns Travel Loyalty?
item.description: Morgan Stanley analysts Ravi Shanker and Jeff Adelson take a look at what the fight for affluent, loyal travelers could mean for banks and airlines.

item.title: Asia’s Race to Power AI
item.description: As AI demand surges, our Asia Energy Analyst Mayank Maheshwari discusses the new multi-trillion-dollar investment cycle to secure the power, fuels, grids and storage that keep modern life running.

item.title: The High Cost of AI Memory
item.description: The Head of our Europe and Asia Technology Team, Shawn Kim, explains how AI’s appetite for memory chips is boosting the cost of everything from data centers to smartphones, with consequences that may reach far beyond the tech industry..

item.title: What New Tariffs Mean for Investors
item.description: Trade policy is once again in the news with the announcement of new tariffs. Our Head of Public Policy Research Ariana Salvatore digs into why tariffs may not be a disruptive factor for markets this time.

item.title: Why Oil Supply May Stay Tight for Months
item.description: Our Global Commodities Strategist Martijn Rats discusses why the restart of oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz may be slower, tighter and messier than the market expects.

item.title: The New AI Credit Playbook
item.description: Chief Fixed Income Strategist Vishy Tirupattur takes a look at how credit markets are adapting to fund the new phase of AI capex.

item.title: When Stocks, Bonds and Oil Move Together
item.description: Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets takes a closer look at potential investment paths when markets appear increasingly synchronized around a few macro themes.

item.title: Pet Industry and the Bite of Higher Costs
item.description: Our U.S. Hardlines, Broadlines and Food Retail Analyst Simeon Gutman explains how affordability and new shopping habits are changing how Americans choose and care for their pets.

item.title: Finding Value in Commercial Real Estate Credit
item.description: Commercial real estate debt is now one of the market’s most avoided asset classes. Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets explains why there may be an opportunity to invest in those securities.

item.title: What Changed After the U.S.-China Summit?
item.description: Our Deputy Global Head of Research Michael Zezas explains why the recent U.S.-China summit may have eased near-term risks, without changing the bigger picture for investors.

item.title: The Battle for the Future of Gaming
item.description: As AI changes the video game industry, Matt Cost, from Morgan Stanley’s U.S. Internet team, takes us through the game play and what could drive the next level of engagement.

item.title: The Rally Is Back, But Risks Are Rising
item.description: The speed of the equity rebound is impressive, but the bigger question for investors is what’s powering it—and what could derail it.

item.title: A Larger, Broader IPO Market Takes Shape
item.description: As IPOs gain momentum in 2026, larger and later stage companies are coming to market across sectors. Financial sponsors, retail investors and multiple capital-raising channels are shaping this year’s equity issuance landscape.

item.title: Asia’s Capex Boom Goes Beyond AI
item.description: Our Chief Asia Economist Chetan Ahya looks at why spending not only on AI, but also on energy and defense, could drive Asia's strongest industrial cycle in decades.

item.title: The New Japan Trade
item.description: The conclusion of our two-part episode from Morgan Stanley and MUFG’s Japan Summit looks at structural shifts in Japan’s economy and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s strategic growth agenda.

item.title: What’s Driving Japan’s Market Momentum
item.description: Recorded live at the Morgan Stanley and MUFG Japan Summit, our Global Chief Economist and Head of Macro Research Seth Carpenter led a discussion on Asia’s exposure to the energy shock and Japan’s bullish outlook.

item.title: Why the UK’s Economy May Surprise Investors Again
item.description: Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets and Chief UK Economist Bruna Skarica discuss why they see a more constructive UK outlook than markets do, despite energy, fiscal and political risks.

item.title: The Case for Staying Bullish on Equities
item.description: Despite recent pressure on stocks, our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson argues that earnings and AI’s impact remain stronger than many investors appreciate.

item.title: How Digital Assets Are Changing Banking
item.description: Our Global Head of Banks and Diversified Finance Research Betsy Graseck explains how digital assets could reshape market infrastructure and how money moves, without overthrowing wholesale banking.

item.title: Investing Through an Uneasy Boom
item.description: Our Chief Cross-Asset Strategist Serena Tang explains why investors should stay constructive in 2026, even as oil prices and geopolitics add volatility.

item.title: 2026 Midyear Investment Outlook: Constructive, Not Complacent
item.description: AI infrastructure investment is boosting the outlook for risk assets, particularly U.S. equities, despite geopolitical risks. Credit markets could face challenges as companies increase bond issuance.

item.title: Growth Faces an Energy Test
item.description: Our Global Chief Economist and Head of Macro Strategy Seth Carpenter gives his mid-year outlook, highlighting why AI investment and U.S. consumers remain key growth engines amid energy shocks.

item.title: What to Expect From the U.S.-China Summit
item.description: Our Head of Public Policy Research Ariana Salvatore goes through the main topics on the table during the meeting between Presidents Trump and Xi: Taiwan, tariffs and the Iran conflict.

item.title: How Your Body Data Could Reshape Sectors
item.description: Our U.S. Healthcare Analyst Erin Wright discusses how health tracking and preventive diagnostics could influence healthcare costs and different industries, from fitness to retail.

item.title: Activist Investors Are Holding Boards Accountable for AI Strategy
item.description: In recent campaigns, activist investors have challenged companies on their AI strategy, capital allocation and credibility. Here’s what boards should understand—and how management teams can get ahead of AI driven scrutiny.

item.title: Corporate Sustainability Strategies Continue Globally, But Progress Slows
item.description: Global corporates continue to execute their sustainability strategies, as macroeconomic uncertainty, regulation, investor expectations and climate risk shape the agenda.

item.title: Why AI Funding Is So Price-Insensitive
item.description: Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets explains the economic theory behind the unwavering spending on AI infrastructure.

item.title: The New Playbook for Real Estate Net Lease Investing
item.description:
As real estate values reset and cap rates widen, net lease is back in focus—but the approach has changed. Ron Kamdem and Hank D’Alessandro explain.

Hank D’Alessandro is not a member of Morgan Stanley’s Research Department. Unless otherwise indicated, his views are his own and may differ from the views of the Morgan Stanley Research Department and from the views of others within Morgan Stanley.

item.title: How Long Can Markets Ignore the Oil Supply Shock?
item.description: Despite the historical energy disruption from the Iran conflict, stocks are back to record highs. Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets and our Head of Commodity Research Martijn Rats discuss different views and fundamentals driving markets.

item.title: Founder Survey Reveals Insights on Growth, Capital and the Path to Liquidity
item.description: Founders are broadening capital strategies, embracing interim liquidity solutions such as tender offers, and paying close attention to IPO readiness, according to Morgan Stanley’s Founder Survey.

item.title: AI’s Shift From Thinking to Taking Action
item.description: Our Head of Europe and Asia Technology Research Shawn Kim discusses AI’s move from passive chatbots to active agents—and how this influences tech supply chains.

item.title: Why Stocks Keep Rallying
item.description: Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson explains the factors behind stock gains across sectors.

item.title: AI and Jobs: What Data and History Say
item.description: Our Global Chief Economist and Head of Macro Research Seth Carpenter discusses whether the economy can adapt fast enough to turn AI into a productivity boom rather than a labor market shock.

item.title: The Metric Taking Over Earning Season
item.description: Capital spending usually signals how a company is positioning itself for the future. Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets explains why this metric is getting more attention from investors.

item.title: Midterm Elections, Affordability and the Fed
item.description: Still six months out, the U.S. midterm elections are likely to influence government initiatives to deal with higher energy costs. Our Head of Public Policy Research Ariana Salvatore and Global Chief Economist Seth Carpenter discuss how the Congress and the Fed might react.

item.title: AI’s Next Big Leap
item.description:
Tom Wigg and Stephen Byrd discuss the accelerating pace of AI breakthroughs, the forces driving them and why the next phase of development may look very different from anything we’ve seen so far.

 

Tom Wigg is a member of Morgan Stanley’s Institutional Equity Division and is not a member of Morgan Stanley’s Research Department. Unless otherwise indicated, his views are his own and may differ from the views of the Morgan Stanley Research Department and from the views of others within Morgan Stanley.

item.title: Can Stock Momentum Hold Up?
item.description: Major U.S. stock indexes have rebounded sharply in recent weeks. Our CIO and Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Mike Wilson discusses the fundamentals that could support the continuation of the bull market.

item.title: Warsh’s Plan to Change the Fed
item.description: Kevin Warsh, President Trump’s nominee for the next Fed Chair, testified in front of the Senate earlier this week. Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets presents key takeaways from the two-and-a-half-hour testimony.

item.title: The Hidden Toll of Tariffs
item.description: Our Global Chief Economist and Head of Macro Research Seth Carpenter asks Mayank Phadke, a member of his team, to give up an update on tariffs and their real cost to the U.S. economy.

item.title: How Individual Investors Are Approaching Sustainable Investing in 2026
item.description: Sentiment remains strong globally, even as average portfolio allocations edged down slightly. Expectations about returns continue to shape investment decisions.
